text_fidelity_a:
ALPS Mountaineering Meramac 4-Person Tent, Sage/Rust Having had, and liking, several ALPS Mountaineering products ([[ASIN:B004R7L7YU ALPS OutdoorZ Commander Backpack, 5250 Cubic Inches]] and [[ASIN:B006H1YL1U ALPS Mountaineering Stuff Sack]]), and being in the market for another tent, I chose the 4 Person tent knowing that (1) I'll never really need it to hold four people and (2), I will not be carrying this in my backpack. This tent was specifically bought for car camping.

I like that it has a carry case instead of stuff sack. I'm not quite certain why, but this just seems to make more sense to me. I'm probably less likely to forget the case. I'm also happy with the set up. Instead of sliding poles through a sleeve as several of my other tents do, this is simply a connect the poles, lay them out, put the ends into the stoppers and clip the tent to the poles. It's much easier going up and, if you were in a good location, you really wouldn't need to put in pegs and could freestand.

The one thing about this tent that I didn't like or understand is why they were put a pole under the fly and have you pull the fly up and over the erected tent like that. Honestly, I looked and looked at the instructions and did not see a single thing about that. YouTube came to the rescue in the form of "Mr. Tent".

Since I've not had the opportunity to actually test it out of yet - sure I could put it up in the livingroom and have "Camp InHouse", and I may yet do that, I'm going to leave this review as is and modify it in the future should the need arise. I do not anticipate any problems because I am familiar with the brand, style of tent and my expected usage.
text_fidelity_b: ALPS Mountaineering Meramac 4-Person Tent, Sage/Rust

text_fidelity_a:
Champion Eclipse Graphite Complete Pickleball Set | Includes 3.0 Portable Net System + 4 Graphite Pickleball Paddles + 4 Outdoor Pickleballs + Pickleball Duffel Bag + USAPA Rulebook After weeks of bad weather and then surgery (and recovery) and then more bad weather, we finally had a day we could get out with this Champion Eclipse Graphite Complete Pickleball Set and give it a try. We did end up trying the paddles separate from the net (long story), but find both parts of this set really good and when we do get the chance to actual use the paddles with the net, it’ll be great. For what my wife and I consider a “beginner” and/or at home set, this is a really nice offering.

First, the “tools.” This set includes a bag (for these items), Rulebook, 4 paddles, 4 balls. All beginner level, if you get into pickle ball you’ll likely find yourself looking to upgrade, but for the backyard, for beginners, for kids or adults getting into this fast growing sport, this Champion Eclipse Graphite Complete Pickleball Set will get you off on the right foot. My wife and I are technically beginners, but we have played (not a lot), but we already do prefer longer paddles - yet we found these were good for practice. The weight is not bad, and overall they worked great. For adults or kids, they should work fine. The balls work. We play outdoors and they were fine for us. We actually got this set (primarily) for the net. The community where we live has 2 tennis courts, but also a lot of people who play tennis (most communities we’ve lived in no one does). So we wanted to have something we could take to a local park or parking lot and be able to play (we will return to club play when this Covid stuff... gets better). But we’ve used these balls and paddle on the tennis courts and they worked fine. The bag for the paddle and balls works well. It’s not top of the line, but it works fine and we’ll keep these in it for a quick grab and go.

The big plus for us was the rule book. Again, we’re only starting out and played some club stuff just before Covid. This is letting us get up to speed ahead of getting back to thing. So thrilled that was included.

The Net: this was what we really got the Champion Eclipse Graphite Complete Pickleball Set for. Again, our tennis courts can fill up when the weather allows and we were not getting any time. So we thought let’s try it. We come away very impressed. The bag it comes in is solid, well made, and while the net is slightly heavy, to us it means the materials are substantial, but not so heavy a lot of people would have an issue. We didn’t weight it, but my wife and I are guessing around 15 - 20 lbs. It did take some time to set up the first time. Working through the steps and matching the pieces - it ended up being really easy, but everything is slow going that first time. I think substantial is the best word here. We have tried a few volleyball and badminton nets and came away underwhelmed or sort of happy. This net is very good. The pieces are metal, well marked, and well designed. We set it up at the park where there was shade (our hot weather state has been off the charts hot), and got it together in less than 10 minutes - that was with undoing things for the first time, such as wrapping. Note; we kept the long plastic bags the longer pieces come in, in tact in order to store them back in each, to keep them from banging around in the bag. All the pieces of the set seem well designed and made. I would say one person could set it up easily. It also seems like, as long as you take care of it, it’ll last. There are black rubber ends to things TIP: keep them and put them back on to protect the pieces in storage.

In the end my wife and I are thrilled - not only to finally get to start using things - but with both the paddle/bag/ball/rules portion of the Champion Eclipse Graphite Complete Pickleball Set and the net part. together or separate, you’ll find a nice beginner and/or family set for a lot of fun. Our use will be varied, but we are happy to have this Champion Eclipse Graphite Complete Pickleball Set.
text_fidelity_b: Champion Eclipse Graphite Complete Pickleball Set | Includes 3.0 Portable Net System + 4 Graphite Pickleball Paddles + 4 Outdoor Pickleballs + Pickleball Duffel Bag + USAPA Rulebook

Solid iron construction with durable vinyl coating to protect floor
Easy-grip classic style wide handle
Build strength and increase endurance during weight-training workouts
Great for beginners and ideal for all kettlebell movements and exercises

It appears there may be a manufacturers warranty on this product, but it is not spelled out. You need to contact the company. It's hard to imagine you would wear this out.

First thing I did was mount the scope and secure to a picatinny rail. After mounting, I used the adjustment screw on top of the scope for elevating the up or down setting. I also used the adjustment screw setting on the left side of scope to zero in the laser. You can do this for up to 100 yards away but make sure you’re on a flat secure surface. text_fidelity_a:
Ameriwood Home Jacob Laptop Cart, Cherry Update: Fixed the wobble: I found a board in the shed about the width of the other leg, cut one end at the same angle as the desk, painted it cherry and bam! No more wobble at all.
I read all the negative reviews and though they do have a point, but for my use, this works, and I like it. If it doesn't hold up over time I'll update my review.
Pros:
*price is right
*easy assembly
*looks nice
*Allows me to adjust my chair high enough that my legs are at a 90 degree fold which is much more comfortable than having chair too low at my regular desk.
*Having my screen at eye level and tilted really helps my neck, especially since I can't type without looking at the keyboard.
Cons:
*Yes, a little wobbly
*not easy to adjust height if you will regularly want to do so.

To address some of the wobble concerns, the individual components are sturdy, where the desk part slips into the base is where the wobble comes from. I took a plastic "wobble wedge" (available on Amazon) and secured it in the gap, not a perfect fix, but improved the situation. Use real tools to tighten all the bolts and screws, not the tools included in package.
I also used a common plastic door jam to wedge under the uneven wheel.
I do data entry on a calendar, I type for 30 seconds at a time in between calls. When my hands are on the computer, I try to keep the heels of my hands steady, too much hand motion will create a slight wobble. If you are using this for a business where you type long emails or are a student writing papers, you might want to invest in something sturdier. I've seen ones in stores for $130 that are no better than this one.
text_fidelity_b: Ameriwood Home Jacob Laptop Cart, Cherry

text_fidelity_a:
Axiom Streamliner Road DLX Racks I am pleased with the rack. However, it did not come with any instructions. I was able to figure it out anyway. You have to take off your rear brake and mount the bracket on the brake bolt between the brake and the frame. You put your wheel skewer through the holes on the bottom. Note that this makes it annoying to remove the rear wheel.

As another reviewer noted, the bracket needs to be bent in order to fit. This is unavoidable because different bicycles have different frame geometry. It is easy to bend with pliers and I had it bent correctly in about 2 minutes.

Note also that it is a narrow rack and is meant for mounting bags or baskets on the sides. Mounting to the top is iffy. (I mounted a basket to the top anyway, using enough zip ties to make sure it won't move).

This rack is much more securely mounted than my old one, which was mounted with p-clips. It is also much lower and closer to the wheel which helps keep the weight down low so it doesn't affect handling as much.

If you have a road bike, you can definitely use this rack to increase your cargo capacity. I was looking for something like this for a while and I'm glad someone makes it.
text_fidelity_b: Axiom Streamliner Road DLX Racks

text_fidelity_a:
Kuat Dirtbag This mount was exactly what I needed. I had built a fork mount roof rack for my fatbike out of an old Thule rack. I originally used a sunlite fatbike fork mount, but after the nut fell off that mount and not being able to buy a new one, I had to replace the whole unit.
I bought the 135mm X 9mm fork mount. This fits fatbike forks with 135mm spacing with quick release. I have. 2014 Specialized fatboy and it fits perfect. It won't fit through axle forks like the Bluto which are 150mm X 15mm. This mount does not come with a 135mm skewer, so you can either buy an extra, or use the one from your wheel. The rear wheels of most mountain bikes is 135mm so they are pretty common and affordable. The fork rests on two short metal tubes the same size as your axle, and just like your axle the skewer goes through the metal tubes to anchor your fork to the mount. This design is ingenious. There has been mention of misalignment in other reviews, mine did not have that problem. If the skewer falls off or someone steals it, you only have to replace the skewer and not the whole unit. This mount is good quality and should last awhile.
text_fidelity_b: Kuat Dirtbag

text_fidelity_a:
Franklin Sports Automatic Pickleball Launcher Machine - ProShot Pickleball Tosser for Pickleball Practice + Training - Portable Pickleball Thrower + Ball Server - Pickleball Training Equipment + Aid [[VIDEOID:8f817e3757cba9acee2517fb67b2d7f0]] This Franklin Sports Automatic Pickleball Launcher Machine seems like it's going to be a good tool as my wife and I as we look to improve our game together or independently.

Every product we've gotten from Franklin has been a good one, so when we had the chance to grab this Franklin Sports Automatic Pickleball Launcher Machine we took it. Not only is the brand - to our experience - good and reliable, it has good longevity. So would this Franklin Sports Automatic Pickleball Launcher Machine stand up to that expectation? So far it seems like it will. We've only had it a short time - and due to weather, only recently gotten to actually try it. But what we are experiencing is impressive.

1. It comes in a great box (good enough for gifting), unassembled. You'll find the base in tact, but the scoop track for holding balls will need to be put together. As I have little to no patience my wife is the one who usually assembles in our house - I'm on stand by for instruction deciphering and a lending hand. In this case we both found the print a bit small - in fact, an issue many manufacturers are having seems to be providing large enough print for even the best eyes - so we have learned to take pictures and blow them up. In this case, we found the instructions average at best. We figured it out, but it took too much time for what we consider "good instructions," and the size (which yes, it does matter - especially in a sport taken up by so many GenX and Baby Boomers). Lastly, there is nothing that really talks about HOW the unit works and WHAT you can do to help improve your game with it. Again, many over 40 are taking up America's fastest growing sports - it would be nice if Franklin considered the demographics for future improvements.

2. The battery compartment: you'll need a tiny Philips head screwdriver to undo to the two tiny screws. There is nothing included. We also wish companies would consider that this kind of access is difficult and annoying: 1. you'll need a very specific, small size of screw driver, 2. the screws were VERY TIGHT in there and we needed to use a kitchen gripping rubber cloth to even undo the screws, 3. WHY can't it be the same kind of slide on cover often found on things like TV remote controls for easier access?

You'll need 4 D sized batteries and while we've only just gotten to use this Franklin Sports Automatic Pickleball Launcher Machine, we are guessing we'll be switching out new batteries often enough that this type of access will grow tiring - quickly. This is our big CON for this Franklin Sports Automatic Pickleball Launcher Machine - a FAR BETTER battery compartment design for access would make this a TRUE 5 STAR - though we decided to give it the fill 5 anyways - this IS enough to warrant us considering dropping it to 4.

3. The unit has two on/off switches - we are assuming one for each motor, with one being on each side of the shooter.

4. There is enough room for a good amount of balls. As you can see in the pictures, you won't be refilling too often, but we can see where even for two people using it, one can refill while the other practices.

5. There is a slight "noise" to the motors, but nothing annoying or loud - meaning you won't disturb the neighbors.

6. It takes several seconds for the ball to shoot once engaged with the launcher, but once it goes... look out! It's got some great power! We've only used on one speed-setting, but it was fun.

7. The unit overall is not too heavy nor takes up too much space. Meaning you will likely find it easy to carry with to a court and for storing won't need that much room. At the same time, it is sufficiently heavy so as not to be even remotely worrisome that it'll fall over or easily be knocked over. And while it will take up room in our closet or porch, it'll set out of the way as well.

But not likely for taking to the community or park or the like. But it is a great feature and one we'll - hopefully one day - take advantage of on our own home court (one can dream).

In the end we are impressed by the Franklin Sports Automatic Pickleball Launcher Machine and feel like we're going to get some great usage out of. We were getting frustrated as we waited to have the chance to use it, and once we got out there, we were proven correct: it's fun and it'll be a great addition to our learning and improving our pickle ball game. Who do we think it's for? Anyone, young or old, beginner-intermediate-even advanced level, allowing for one to improve their game while having fun, alone or with a partner. Yes, we're happy to have this Franklin Sports Automatic Pickleball Launcher Machine.

text_fidelity_a:
Bicycle Computer Wireless Speedometer, Big Number Display Waterproof Automatic Wake-up Stopwatch with LCD Backlight, Speed Distance Time Measure Temperature Consumption Cycling Accessories I bought this to replace a Specialized computer that only lasted a few years, regardless of battery changes.

The Good:
1. It's relatively inexpensive.
2. It's wireless (between the wheel sensor and the computer), which is *amazing* at this price.
3. The display is decent.
4. I prefer two-button over one-button bike computers.
5. If you have a very oddball configuration, it can handle it.

The Bad:
Oh my, let's count the ways.
1. Somewhat unclear manual
2. Incomplete manual - missing super-common bicycle tire sizes. I bought this for a Trek DS8 commuter bike, which has a 700x38. Not listed.
3. Their solution to that? Roll the bike carefully along the ground and measure it. Yeah, right. I guessed, and will work it out later.
4. Unrealistic specs. The manual is clear that the magnet must come within 5mm (1/2cm or less than 1/5th of an inch) of the sensor. Which is not realistic. Compounding this, their magnet's shape requires it be mounted where spoke cross... which many bikes have another mounting point at.
Fortunately, it isn't really that picky.
5. To change the computer mount orientation, you must unscrew four-to-five (seriously, depending on desired orientation) tiny itty bitty screws, re-orient, and replace all or nearly all (seriously... you may no longer have access to some holes) of them.
6. The display is decent, but it really doesn't resemble the one in the photos. In reality, it's much lower contrast (and, of course, not as large as the photos imply, but normal size for a bike computer.)
7. You get, seriously, about 15 seconds after inserting the battery to choose MPH vs KPH... but... much of that time is spent getting the battery door back on and flipping it over. I don't think there's a way to do it other than initially. (To switch it at that point, hit the RIGHT side button. Oddly, the "Mode" button doesn't change modes between K and M, and it doesn't stand for Miles ;)... if you hit M, you have to take out the battery and try again.)

That sounds pretty bad. But all of this is first-time-setup stuff. It really is a VERY nice bike computer even for much more than the price. I'll provide more updates after I've calibrated the tire correctly.
text_fidelity_b: Bicycle Computer Wireless Speedometer, Big Number Display Waterproof Automatic Wake-up Stopwatch with LCD Backlight, Speed Distance Time Measure Temperature Consumption Cycling Accessories

text_fidelity_a:
Niceday Steppers for Exercise, Stair Stepper with Resistance Bands, Mini Stepper with 300LBS Loading Capacity, Hydraulic Fitness Stepper with LCD Monitor [[VIDEOID:9cd18f2d8b61d1fb4584e3a87364b212]] My wife and I work at home and already had a stepper unit, but she had been wanting one for her work space, rather than have to carry the slightly larger and bit heavier one I use in the main area of the house, back and forth to her space. So when I had the chance to grab this Niceday Steppers for Exercise, Stair Stepper with Resistance Bands I took it and so far, she's very pleased.

The Niceday Steppers for Exercise, Stair Stepper with Resistance Bands comes pretty much assembled. There are the handles at the end of the resistance band you can place onto the unit (so far she has not done so), so there is that "assembly," but for stepping it's pretty much out of the box and go. You do have to adjust the resistance - we seems more about the height of the steps rather than how much resistance it gives you, but that is easy enough - turn the orange dial underneath either clockwise or counterclockwise to where you're comfortable. I will say, it took a few tries - the steps are set VERY high out of the box, so we played with and got it adjusted after a few tries - to our preferred setting. Again, she is set to use this as she works at her home office adjustable height desk, so that's in the corner of the bedroom - already a full space - and has it tucked in a corner when not in use. The weight of the unit is good and easy enough to move. It is indeed lighter than the other one we had that she formerly had to move back and forth when she wanted it - again, for space we were not keeping it in there as well as for use while working out in the other room. She hasn't used the handles - which we both feel like they are good, but could be better. The handles themselves are thinner and not 100% comfortable for longer sessions. They are compact and don't take up much room, but she's planning to use this while working, so no real need for them, but also, not sure she'd find them comfortable - but this is based on simply holding them in the hand, not actual use. The surface of the Niceday Steppers for Exercise, Stair Stepper with Resistance Bands is raised in bumps for traction. I tried it with no shoes - it's doable, but I'd say not for a full workout. My wife tried the first time in slippers and was fine. She does use shoes for any workouts. The traction is good all around. The steps give a solid, good amount of resistance and give one the burn you're looking for. There is a battery included for the timer/counter, but we both realized later it was still sitting where we placed it to not loose it and the stepper was keeping track - so it came with one in it. The stepper makes next to no noise so there is no worry about having to talk over a phone call. The one thing that my wife and I disagree on between the unit we had and this one: the track of the step. On the previous stepper we already had, the track of stepping traces a path that moves the foot outwards at the bottom, inwards as it goes up. I like this for the way my step/hips work - she does not. This Niceday Steppers for Exercise, Stair Stepper with Resistance Bands tracks the steps straight up and down, making it more comfortable for my wife, less so for myself.

In the end the Niceday Steppers for Exercise, Stair Stepper with Resistance Bands is a nice stepper, has a good solid balance, feels high at first, but can be somewhat adjusted, and steps well. The workout is good. We have different feels on the track, but for my wife, this Niceday Steppers for Exercise, Stair Stepper with Resistance Bands is right on the money. We are happy to have it.
text_fidelity_b: Niceday Steppers for Exercise, Stair Stepper with Resistance Bands, Mini Stepper with 300LBS Loading Capacity, Hydraulic Fitness Stepper with LCD Monitor

text_fidelity_a:
TurnOnSport Magnesium Fire Starter Survival Kit - Flint Steel Fire Starter & Compass - Ferro Rods Fire Striker Hiking Whistle Paracord Lanyard Black Fire starter is great. Whistle is great. Compass not so great.

This works as described for starting fires. The instructions are easy to follow. Scrape some magnesium onto your kindling. It takes a fair amount to get a big enough fire going, so keep scraping! Then quickly slide the striker along the rod to send sparks into the scrapings. I first did this with a paper towel so that I could see how much material was being scraped off. Due to the amount of scrapings needed, it might be best to buy magnesium shavings separately, but that adds bulk to your go bag.

Striking technique: I found that a motion similar to striking a match works best. I put the striker/scraper against the rod but pointed away from the kindling, with my thumb putting pressure on the striker. A flip of wrist slides the striker firmly against the rod and ends up pointing toward the kindling, sending sparks into your scrapings. This can be done without removing the striker from the lanyard.

The case serves as a handle for the magnesium rod, making it easier to hold onto while scraping and striking. The case protects the magnesium rod while not starting fires.

The case also has a small storage compartment that has a hinged rubber stopper/seal. There is no mention of this in the instructions nor on the item description. Another reviewer indicated that the compartment could hold wooden matches. I think that's a great idea. I tested with full-sized kitchen matches and found I could fit four, but only if I cut the matches to be a little shorter. Perhaps a better use of the compartment would be to store some magnesium shavings. It would at least be enough for one or two fires.

The whistle is loud and very high pitched. No doubt it will carry far in an emergency. It takes a little more effort than I expected. At first I thought it did not work. But then I really blew into it and sent a piercing note into the neighborhood.

Compass does not work well. I consider such glue-on compasses as gimmicks from the start and therefore no stars off. In this case the compass will not level itself to allow free spinning. If you fuss with it enough it may eventually point approximately north. It is better to invest in a quality compass.
text_fidelity_b: TurnOnSport Magnesium Fire Starter Survival Kit - Flint Steel Fire Starter & Compass - Ferro Rods Fire Striker Hiking Whistle Paracord Lanyard Black

Freeze Dried Sliced Strawberries by Nutristore | Pack of 2 | Healthy Snack | Emergency Survival Bulk Food Storage | Amazing Taste & Quality | 25 Year Shelf Life These strawberries are beyond delicious! These big #10 (one gallon) cans of freeze dried fruit are IDEAL if you are new to using freeze dried fruits or if you want to put away a couple cans for your family in case of emergency but you don't want to spend $150 on a 6 can case plus shipping from somewhere else. (You simply cannot beat Amazon Prime!)

• • • #10 cans typically hold 12 cups of food and about 11 cups of freeze dried fruits and veggies • • •

It is hard to find information about how much food is actually in a #10 can and have it be accurate enough that you can plan your meals. When filled to the brim with something like rice, the #10 cans hold 12 cups. But freeze dried food is light and not compacted, with air space between the dry pieces so you get about 11 cups (bananas) to 11.25 cups (strawberries and raspberries) in a big can like this. The cans are "full", the difference is simply air space between the fruit pieces. (To be safe, always assume there are 11 cups per #10 can of freeze dried fruits and veggies. I have found this to be accurate and a great way to calculate how much you have stored.)

Now let's talk about how yummy the food is! As I took pictures I could hardly stop my 9 year old son from grabbing handfuls of strawberries behind my back as I tried to snap a quick photo. (The bowl of strawberries was dumped straight into his mouth mere seconds after I got that picture!) The fruit is positively DELICIOUS for snacking straight from the can!

We live in Houston and personally lived through Hurricane Ike in 2008. At the time my son was 18 months old and I would have given anything - ANYTHING - to have these freeze dried strawberries to have offered him. Grocery stores were picked clean the day before the storm. Some of the grocery stores flooded and most of them had damage to roofs, glass doors and building structures from being hit by flung tree branches, fence pieces and debris. We went 12 days without electricity in our home. Grocery stores were without power for the first 5 or 6 days and stayed closed for about a week in our area as they had to be cleaned up before reopening. It was almost 3 weeks after the storm before stores were restocked with fresh produce beyond a few local items like tomatoes and jalapeños. Please, take the advice from someone who has lived through a natural disaster and invest in freeze dried fruits and veggies for your family. Everything in our refrigerators and freezers were ruined by day 2 without power and we still had 10 days to go. The only thing you have to rely on is what you have on your pantry shelves. That is it. These cans will keep for 25 years unopened and truly are a wise investment.

So, since I have been through a natural disaster, I have learned how to bake with freeze dried food since I still live in Houston and may have to deal with another storm in the future. These strawberries did GREAT and I'm going to include the recipe I used so you can have success with them, too. It is wise to open and try the food you are storing but since this company gave several reviewers like myself a discount to test their products, this work has been done for you. You can simply store the cans of food knowing it is superior quality. (I have purchased and used Thrive brand fruits and these taste identical to theirs! In my opinion these strawberries were even better quality.)

• Strawberry Chocolate Chip Muffins •
--> This recipe also works with freeze dried blueberries or other freeze dried fruits
1/4 cup butter, softened
1/3 cup sugar
1 egg, beaten
1/2 cup milk (a small can of evaporated milk is fine to use)
1 cup flour (up to 1.5 cups depending on humidity; batter should be a thick muffin batter)
1 and 1/2 tsp baking powder
1/2 cup freeze dried strawberries (or raspberries or other fruit) rehydrated in 1/2 cup water with the excess liquid drained off
1/2 cup milk chocolate chips

Preheat oven to 400°. Cream butter and sugar. Add the egg and mix well. Add flour alternately with splashes of milk and combine until a thick batter has formed and all ingredients are incorporated. Gently fold in rehydrated fruit. Spoon into 12 paper lined baking cups, filling halfway to 3/4ths full. Bake for 20 minutes or until tops begin to turn golden.

• Tip •
The leftover powder at the bottom of each can is AWESOME for making strawberry butter or adding to oatmeal to make your own fruit and cream flavor. If nothing else, dump the powder in your pancake batter. Don't let the powder go to waste, it is delicious!

Also, if you want to know about the countries of origin on the fruits, this was posted on the seller's FAQ page: "We source our Nutristore foods from some of the following countries: USA, Canada, Ecuador, Greece, Costa Rica, Uruguay, Argentina, Serbia, New Zealand, India, Poland, Mexico & Chile. [We] no longer source foods from China."

I was very fortunate to be able to purchase this pack of freeze dried strawberries at a discount so I could try it, eat it and bake with it before writing a review. I hope that by sharing my photos and experience that you are able to make the best buying decision for your own family! Hugs from Houston!
text_fidelity_b: Freeze Dried Sliced Strawberries by Nutristore | Pack of 2 | Healthy Snack | Emergency Survival Bulk Food Storage | Amazing Taste & Quality | 25 Year Shelf Life

text_fidelity_a:
BROADREAM Dinosaur Toys Headlamp, T-Rex Kids Dinosaur Toys for Girls Boys Camping, Hiking, Reading in Dark,3 Bright Illumination Modes, Loud Dino Roars, Great Kid Toys Dinosaurs, Christmas, BD Gift [[VIDEOID:2187373aca733f879c0dd8e6a9bc255]] This a fun headlamp designed primarily for kids who like dinosaurs and adventure.

The LED lamp is housed inside a rather large plastic T. rex head. You turn it on by squeezing the open jaws together slightly. The moderately bright light comes on, the eyes light up red, and the dinosaur makes several loud roaring sounds (see attached video). Another squeeze of the jaws and the light turns off.

The adjusable headstrap is decorated with stylized reptilian footprints, in a color scheme that suggests lizard scales. There's a strap down the middle that rides on top of the wearer's head, in addition to the band that goes around your head, to support the weight of the dinosaur and its electronics.

I like that the unit comes with AAA batteries installed. Just pull out the plastic strip that keeps the unit shut off in its package, and it's ready to go. The original batteries probably won't last long, so plan to replace them, preferably with NiMH rechargeables, if you or your young explorers will be using the headlamp much.

This lamp is intended to be a functional novelty, something between a toy and a tool. It doesnt have the brightest light or the most durable housing, among available headlamps, and I'd advise against testing its ability to resist water, especially submersion. The roaring noise could be annoying if someone is trying to use the lamp in a dark room or tent when others are trying to sleep. I do wish that there was some way to turn off the sound. The sound effects may be useful, though, for parents keeping tabs on their young explorer's nighttime activities.

The colorful stripes and loud roar are fanciful embellishments that will likely appeal to young explorers, but I doubt that anyone would defend them as accurate or realistic. Neither of those features are preserved in the fossil record that we have for dinosaurs, so we probably can't say they are inaccurate, either. The thing is intended to fun. Just go with it.

Let me know if anything in my review was helpful.
text_fidelity_b: BROADREAM Dinosaur Toys Headlamp, T-Rex Kids Dinosaur Toys for Girls Boys Camping, Hiking, Reading in Dark,3 Bright Illumination Modes, Loud Dino Roars, Great Kid Toys Dinosaurs, Christmas, BD Gift

text_fidelity_a: Campbell Hausfeld RP410099AV Home Inflation System My title pretty much says it all. The connector makes a good contact, and you lose little air putting it on or taking it off.  I've read of other evaluators who said their units lost lots of air, especially when removing the connector from the valve tip.  My only slight problem is the unit has a nice decent length air line which fits into the plastic housing.  There is a little piece of plastic that goes on top to keep the air line in the unit when not in use.  However, if you wish to leave the air line out, it is really easy to lose this plastic cover.  It's no big deal, but I hate losing parts, even non essential ones. Posstscript:  Unit basically stopped functioning after 6 months; the motor was burning up (you could smell it), and I was afraid to run it for fear of fire or other probelms. I don't think it is built to last, but when it is working, it does fine; the problem is it simply does not last. I  never abused unit and used it sparingly.  I am afraid (at least this one) does not hold up well. I bought a unit from Home Depot called "Husky" that has a two year warranty on it; this unit has held up for over a year (still all right).
text_fidelity_b: Campbell Hausfeld RP410099AV Home Inflation System

The claim about 1 million pulls, at least on mine, fell short. The Kevlar Cord broke after 14 months (and I really don't use it that much other than 2 times a day 5 days a week). I measured the cord to where the break is and it only measures 27". This leads me to believe that either 1. the cord isn't as long as advertised, or 2. (and more likely) the break happened mid way in the cord. It makes me wonder about the Kevlar claim.

This is the only reason for the lower rating. I will look at getting another very soon (don't know if I'll get another Key-Bak or something else), the price is a little high but I guess 11 to 15 dollars every year isn't going to kill me.
text_fidelity_b: KEY-BAK SECURIT Heavy Duty Retractable Key Holder with a Retractable Kevlar Cord Secures Keys, Gear

Ibera Bicycle Seatpost-Mounted Commuter Carrier Rack or Rack and Trunk Bag Combo, Regular Size Rack Only, Regular Size Combo, Compact Size Combo This rack is a tad on the heavy side for me. I like the old small tube aluminum racks that fit on road bikes, etc, but they don't have to take the stresses of being cantilevered from the seat tube as the only mount.
I was dissapointed the clamp did not get tight on my 1.07" diameter cross bike's seat tube, even with the rubber pad.

The good news is I figured out how to put the unit together myself, without directions, and the shorn screw holes were not vital for the operation of the machine or visible unless you look closely.
Assembly:
There are three screws with a plastic cap. Two are big and one is small. The large ones go behind the monitor and at the bottom of the unit in the front. The small one goes on the left side of the unit in the front. There are two plastic covers that go at the foot of the back of the unit on each side. They screw in with four screws. (Again, I could only use two screws because two of the screw holes were stripped.) That is it for assembly. It was relatively easy to assemble, and the unit works well. I am 5’9” and don’t fall off of it. I like that there are no rails on the side to run into. The price was perfect for my budget, and overall, I am very happy because I hate going to the gym, so, this is a great relatively inexpensive alternative.
text_fidelity_b: Confidence Power Plus Motorized Fitness Treadmill White

text_fidelity_a: Olgaa Chin Up Bar Pull Up Bar Doorway Pullup Chin up Bar Home, Multifunctional Portable Dip bar Fitness It's not great.  My husband had another one of these for many years and I wanted replace it with something newer.  But very clearly, the quality has diminished.  First, there was no instructions provided - and the pictures on the box did not fully match the items in the box.  Second, the holes weren't fully perforated, so my husband had to sand it off.  Third, they changed the screws to just nuts and bolts instead of end caps.  Fourth, the supplied tools are so low quality that the wrench was 'stripped' through the installation.  Fifth, the thing is significantly lighter than the other pull-up bar that my husband had previously - indicating that it's not as sturdy.  Lastly, and most importantly, the whole thing just seems WEAK.  In the prior model, when my husband did a pull up, the middle barely made any movement.  In this new one, not only does the middle bow, but the entire thing bends.  He only weigh 178 pounds, but this thing gives him safety concerns.  Therefore we will be giving it away to someone who weighs significantly less.
text_fidelity_b: Olgaa Chin Up Bar Pull Up Bar Doorway Pullup Chin up Bar Home, Multifunctional Portable Dip bar Fitness

text_fidelity_a:
Howard Leight by Honeywell Impact Sport Sound Amplification Electronic Shooting Earmuff I was impressed by the popularity and reviews of these earmuffs so I bought them as my first pair. They are well-built and very comfortable. I really like how it reduces noise above 82db while amplifying conversational level noise (when that feature is turned on). However, I find that they don't give me enough noise reduction from firearms at indoor ranges. Particularly larger caliber guns. I end up wearing the soft in-the-ear plugs under these as well.

I ended up buying another set of earmuffs that have a noise reduction rating (NRR) of 30, but they aren't electronic like these. These are rated at NRR 22. I wish I could find a reasonably priced electronic set with a high NRR.

These are perfect for outdoor use, but questionable for indoor. Certainly not enough for me.
text_fidelity_b: Howard Leight by Honeywell Impact Sport Sound Amplification Electronic Shooting Earmuff
